gates.evidence: The surface is s11 (Account Menu Sidebar), which manages account settings and saved articles, away from any sensitive news topics.
The reward is '10 News Credits', a virtual currency earned for playing a 15-second game; no real-world cash or click/install incentives are present.
The proposal uses a positive streak mechanic ('keep your streak alive') and avoids forced ads, fake timers, or 'support us' copy.
The storyboard and storyboard caption (offer phase) describe a Simula rewarded game invitation with a 'Play Now' CTA.
The offer body explicitly states: 'Play a 15-second game with AOL to earn 10 News Credits'.
An equally legible 'No thanks' button is included, and the storyboard indicates the user remains in s11 upon decline.
The trigger occurs upon opening the Account Menu Sidebar (s11), a static utility surface with no streaming AI or active article generation.
Eligibility is restricted to 'Non-signed-in users and signed-in non-subscribers'.

scores.evidence: The proposal uses a 'Daily Reading Streak' in a hub (s11). While proactive, it is disconnected from the immediate 'moment of need' on the article feed, scoring lower than reactive refills.
The streak mechanic feels native to a news habit app. It creates a new scarcity (News Credits) rather than degrading the existing free reading experience.
The reward is capped at one per day and is described as a 'sampling mechanic'. It is gated to non-payers and includes a 10% holdout experiment.
Code-computed economics show a reward cost to serve of $0.0000 against a gross revenue of $0.0090–$0.0150 per view.
The trigger is the Account Menu Sidebar (m10/s11), which the digest identifies as an 'occasional' reach moment, far lower than the core news feed loops.
The proposal maps clearly to SIM-RWD and uses a simple UI patch in an existing sidebar, though grounding errors in IDs increase complexity.
The proposal uses app-specific terms like 'Account Menu Sidebar' and screen IDs (s11), and attempts to link to economy items (though it fails grounding on e42).
Includes an explicit daily cap of 1 and a 1440-minute cooldown, ensuring no nagging occurs.
Features a clearly defined D7 Retention primary KPI, session/click-through guardrails, and a user-level randomization holdout plan.

requiredChanges: Correct the grounding error for the economy item; e42 on s02 is the 'Brandi Glanville' price signal, not a native ad.
Verify the existence of e36 on s11, as s11 is not fully defined in the digest's screen list.
